name: Global Maximum Disguise
description: The local pairwise requirement (that adjacent nodes must have different values) is replaced by a global sum condition. The required total is exactly the theoretical maximum possible sum of the polynomial $6x - x^2$ where $x = p_u + p_v$. This forces every local term to its maximum (which occurs only when $p_u + p_v = 3$), cleanly reducing to bipartite 2-coloring. Models that rely on surface pattern matching will fail to bridge the global sum to the strict local constraint, preventing them from recognizing the bipartite shortcut.
